title: Playbooks can't read the vault when an agent runs them

labels.name: workflow-exception
labels.description: A process step bent on purpose, with the reason on record

milestone.title: Backups · M1: Vaultwarden is backed up in the house
milestone.description: Next items B1 to B3 in the Backups project note (Second_Brain/10_Projects/11_Infrastructure/Backups.md). Done when a snapshot from vaultserv's own nightly timer is listed in its repository on the hub's append-only server, and that snapshot restored into a throwaway Vaultwarden container shows real records and an attachment.

body:
### What happened

An agent ran `ansible-playbook playbooks/hub.yml --check --diff --limit hub` on 2026-10-28 for #73's live rehearsal. The first task failed before reaching any machine:

```
[ERROR]: Task failed: Error processing keyword 'become_pass': The lookup plugin 'ansible.builtin.pipe' failed: lookup_plugin.pipe(bw get password 'keepbreath0 sudo (hub)') returned 1
hub : ok=0 changed=0 unreachable=0 failed=1 skipped=0 rescued=0 ignored=0
```

The same day, the agent setup stopped loading the Bitwarden session key (`BW_SESSION`) into any shell I don't type in, so agents' shells no longer hold it. Every vault read in the playbooks runs `bw get` through an `ansible.builtin.pipe` lookup and needs that key in Ansible's environment. There are fifteen such lookups plus the `bw unlock --check` task in `playbooks/become-password.yml`. They are in `group_vars/all.yml`, `group_vars/droplets.yml`, `host_vars/vaultserv.yml` and the `hub` role. So every playbook fails for an agent, not only the hub play. The scope label is hub because that is where it surfaced and where most of the reads are.

### What I expected

An agent runs any playbook and it reads the vault the way it does from my own terminal, without the session key ever sitting in the agent's shell, in Ansible's environment, or in an Ansible variable.

### How to reproduce

From a non-interactive shell in the dev container, with no `BW_SESSION` exported and the vault unlocked in my own terminal, run `ansible-playbook playbooks/hub.yml --check --diff --limit hub` from `ansible/`.

### Where

keepbreathing-infra `main` at f326730, on the laptop's dev container.

### Done when

A repository lookup plugin, `vault_secret`, in `ansible/lookup_plugins/` and configured in `ansible.cfg`, replaces every `bw get` pipe lookup and the unlock check. It uses an existing `BW_SESSION` if there is one, otherwise it reads the session file itself, and it passes the key only to the `bw` process it starts. Its errors name only the item, the field and the remedy. CI proves this with a fake `bw` and a temporary session file, at normal verbosity and at `-vvv --check --diff`. An agent's `ansible-playbook playbooks/hub.yml --check --diff --limit hub`, with no `BW_SESSION` in its environment, gets past the first play.

Workflow exception: the agent setup says one runner, `vault-run`, is the only way an agent gets a secret. This plugin is a second, narrow reader of the session file, accepted on purpose because that same change broke the playbooks. It also interrupts #73, which waits for it.

Design: one repository lookup plugin, `vault_secret`, called as `lookup('vault_secret', '<item>')` for an item's login password or with `field='<name>'` for exactly one custom field. Each call runs `bw get item` once, with `BW_NOINTERACTION=true` and the key only in that process's environment. A missing session, a locked vault, a stale key, a missing or ambiguous item, and a missing or repeated field each stop the run with a fixed message naming the item, the field and `vu`, never `bw`'s output. The sudo password stays a fact set once per host by `become-password.yml`, and the plugin keeps no cache. The unlock check becomes a check through the same session rule. Rejected: `community.general.bitwarden`, whose `bw_session` option makes the key an Ansible variable that can appear in errors and verbose output; and giving the whole `ansible-playbook` process the key, which every task run on the laptop would inherit.
